SNOWFLAKE WAREHOUSE COST ADVISOR · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER

Why is your Snowflake bill so high?

Paste one row per warehouse — size, credits used, AUTO_SUSPEND, resumes — and see what each warehouse costs, the idle tail an AUTO_SUSPEND of 600 seconds is billing, idle warehouses, warehouses that never suspend and the ready-to-paste ALTER WAREHOUSE command.

Nothing is uploaded and Snowflake is never contacted. The text box is analysed in this browser and never leaves your device. The AUTO_SUSPEND saving is modelled from resumes and idle tails, which is an estimate.

Prefer a CLI, or want a CI check?

Same logic, zero dependencies, one command — reads a file or stdin:

node cli.mjs analyze warehouses.csv
cat warehouses.csv | node cli.mjs analyze -
node cli.mjs analyze warehouses.csv --suspend 120 --fail-on warn   # exit 1 on any waste
node cli.mjs analyze warehouses.csv --json --prices my-prices.json

Get cli.mjs and engine.mjs — Node 18+, nothing to install, no network call. More: Snowflake warehouse cost: AUTO_SUSPEND, idle warehouses and sizing.

What's recognised

InputHandling

Prices are illustrative and dated; edit them with --prices in the CLI. Storage, serverless features, cloud-services credits and multi-cluster warehouses are not modelled.

Common questions

Does this connect to my Snowflake account?

No. It reads the rows you paste and never contacts Snowflake. It cannot see your contract, so every dollar figure is the credits you pasted times a credit price you can edit.

How do I get the numbers?

Credits per warehouse: SUM(CREDITS_USED) grouped by WAREHOUSE_NAME over 30 days from SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.WAREHOUSE_METERING_HISTORY. Size and AUTO_SUSPEND: SHOW WAREHOUSES. Queries and average runtime: ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY. Resumes: RESUME events in WAREHOUSE_EVENTS_HISTORY.

What AUTO_SUSPEND should I use?

Snowflake bills a 60-second minimum each time a warehouse resumes, so 60 seconds is the practical floor. Anything longer pays for idle time after each burst; the default of 600 seconds on a warehouse that wakes hundreds of times a month is a common silent cost. A shorter setting means a colder cache and a short resume wait.

Will a smaller warehouse be cheaper?

Credits per hour halve with each size down, but a long or memory-hungry query can run more than twice as long and cost the same or more. Short queries that do not speed up on a bigger size are the safe candidates. The advisor reports this only as an upper bound and never counts it in the saving.

Is my data uploaded anywhere?

No. The browser page analyses the text in your own browser and never sends it anywhere. The CLI reads a local file or stdin and makes no network call.

snowflake-warehouse-auto-suspend-and-siz.text:
Snowflake Warehouse Cost Advisor · guide

Snowflake warehouse cost: AUTO_SUSPEND, idle warehouses and sizing

Short answer: a warehouse bills credits for every second it runs, whether or not a query is running. Most avoidable spend is idle tail after queries finish, warehouses nobody uses, and sizes bigger than the queries need.

What it costs (illustrative)

  • Credits per hour double with each size: X-Small 1, Small 2, Medium 4, Large 8, X-Large 16, and so on.
  • Price per credit depends on edition and contract; this tool assumes $3.00 and lets you change it.
  • Resume minimum: each resume bills at least 60 seconds.

Where the money is

  • Long AUTO_SUSPEND: every wake-up idles for the whole setting before suspending. Hundreds of dashboard wake-ups a month multiply it.
  • Always-on warehouses: AUTO_SUSPEND off keeps the meter running 24/7, 730 hours a month.
  • Idle warehouses: a retired pipeline or sandbox that still bills.
  • Oversized for short queries: a Large averaging 3-second queries.

Measure and fix

  1. Credits: SELECT warehouse_name, SUM(credits_used) FROM snowflake.account_usage.warehouse_metering_history WHERE start_time >= DATEADD(day, -30, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()) GROUP BY 1;
  2. Size and AUTO_SUSPEND: SHOW WAREHOUSES;. Queries and average runtime from query_history, resumes from warehouse_events_history.
  3. Paste rows into the advisor or run node cli.mjs analyze warehouses.csv. It prints an ALTER WAREHOUSE command per fix.
  4. Change one warehouse at a time and watch query latency for a week before rolling out.

Questions

What AUTO_SUSPEND should a Snowflake warehouse use?

60 seconds is the practical minimum, because every resume bills at least 60 seconds anyway. Longer settings pay for idle time after each burst of queries. Keep a longer value only for a warehouse whose warm cache you rely on and that wakes up rarely.

Why is my Snowflake bill high when queries are fast?

Usually idle time and size, not query work: an AUTO_SUSPEND of 600 seconds on a Large warehouse that wakes 500 times a month bills about 78 hours of idle tail, around 620 credits. Warehouses with AUTO_SUSPEND off run around the clock; a Small is 1,460 credits a month.

Does a smaller warehouse always cost less?

No. Credits per hour halve with each size, but a query that does not scale down can take more than twice as long. Short queries are the safe candidates; try one size down on one warehouse and compare runtimes before rolling it out.
